required_fixes: Clarify operational definition of 'long-value' before any citation: P3_DEEPPATH (value_length 42) and P5_MULTIPARAM (value_length 46) are NOT long per-slot value tests. Per-slot concrete values are orgId=12345 (5 chars), projectId=67890 (5 chars), category=electronics (11), minPrice=100 (3), maxPrice=500 (3). Total string length includes fixed URL scaffolding (v2/api/organizations/, category=, &minPrice=). Re-label these as multi-slot short/medium-per-slot patterns or replace with genuinely long per-slot values (e.g., UUID slugs per slot) before claiming 'long-value savings fail generally'.

Do not cite mean savings 15.99% as passing C5 in isolation or as evidence for savings. Mean is bimodal (P1 +44.44%, P4 +56.72% vs P3 -11.54%, P5 -9.68%, P2 0%) and does not represent the distribution. Report median, per-pattern table, or stratified by slot count instead. C5 PASS does not mitigate C4 FAIL under ALL-must-pass rule.

Fix or stratify C6 (savings increase with value length, r>=0.7). Current r=0.3909 conflates heterogeneous JSON structures (P4 includes headers.Authorization with Bearer, others url-only), total value_length vs per-slot length, and slot count (1 vs 2 vs 3). Recompute correlation stratified by slot count or using per-slot average value length, or pre-register separate hypotheses for single-slot vs multi-slot.

For P2_SLUG breakeven (28 chars, 0% savings) disclose that hypothesis 'saves when >~8 chars' is falsified for this tokenizer/path pattern: 28-char hyphenated slug vs 12-char ${pageSlug} yields equal tokens (21 vs 21) under cl100k_base due to subword tokenization of hyphens, not a clean char-length threshold.

For P3, disclose mismatch between token-measurement literal (first observation uses 100/200, 3 chars) and resolve/bind test literal (expected_bound uses 12345/67890, 5 chars). Token savings for P3 are measured on shorter values than the 'long' label implies, underestimating potential savings for longer IDs. Use consistent concrete values across measurement and pipeline tests or report both.
Provenance: populate missing sha256 for code_paths (kernel.py, models.py, registry.py, tests, run_experiment.py) to enable exact reproduction; current provenance has 4 null hashes.

validity_findings.impact: C4 FAIL (2/5) and C6 low correlation cannot be cited as 'long values fail generally'. Only single-slot genuinely long values (P1 UUID 36, P4 bearer 64) show strong savings; P2 slug 28 breakeven, P3/P5 short-per-slot negative. validity_findings.finding: C6 r=0.3909 <0.7 correctly computed but construct-invalid as pooled test. Value_length mixes total string length (including fixed path/query) with per-slot value length, and literal/parameterized JSON structure mixes url-only (P1-3,P5) with headers+url+method (P4 bearer includes Authorization header). Slot count (1,1,2,1,3) confounds value_length. Ordering by total length P4(64)>P5(46)>P3(42)>P1(36)>P2(28) does not order per-slot length (P4 64, P1 36, P2 28, P5 avg ~5.7, P3 avg 4-5). Correlation of savings with total length is not the prereg falsifier's intended structural relationship (template overhead vs per-slot concrete length).

validity_findings.impact: C6 FAIL is arithmetically correct but scientifically uninformative as pooled. Strong null (r>=0.7) was mis-calibrated for heterogeneous design. Falsification of 'monotonic increase' is valid for this total-length operationalization, but does not falsify per-slot length hypothesis (which would be 2-slot and 3-slot patterns removed, single-slot shows monotonic: 28->0%,36->44%,64->56%). Ceiling must note C6 pooled result is not discriminating.

validity_findings.finding: C5 mean 15.99% >=10% PASS masks bimodal distribution: two large positive outliers (UUID +44.44%, bearer +56.72%) average to +50.58%, two negatives (P3 -11.54%, P5 -9.68%) average to -10.61%, one zero. Median savings is 0% (P2), 3/5 patterns non-positive. Producer correctly notes 'driven by two large savings patterns masking two negative' in observations, but decision rule treats mean as sufficient. Under ALL-must-pass, C5 PASS does not rescue overall verdict, but citation of '15.99% mean savings passes' without distribution is misleading for product economics.

claim_ceiling: FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING per frozen decision_rule (ALL C1-C8 must pass): C4 (2/5 <3/5) and C6 (r 0.3909 <0.7) fail, so the hypothesis 'parameterized saves >=10% mean and >=3/5 patterns and correlates with length' does not survive as a general long-value claim. However, the ceiling is stratified, not general: single-slot genuinely long values SAVE tokens (UUID 36-char +44.44%, bearer 64-char +56.72%) under tiktoken cl100k_base action_template JSON; single-slot medium slug 28-char breakeven (0%); multi-slot patterns with short per-slot values PENALIZE (deep path 2 slots -11.54%, multi-param 3 slots -9.68%) even though total string length is 42-46. Resolve/bind pipeline survives narrowly for manually-registered parameterized mechanisms (7/7 EXECUTABLE with correct params, 7/7 UNKNOWN when missing, _bind correct for 1-3 slots, kernel 3/3 intact) with confidence 0.9 >0.8, GET only, synthetic manual templates, isolated intents, no browser/model/network. No inference to amortized product economics (C-PRODUCT-ECON remains HYPOTHESIS), LLM tokenizers, PUT/POST, cross-site, or distill_parameterized induction. Do not cite mean 15.99% or P3/P5 as evidence that long values fail generally; per-slot length and slot count are the causal factors. Max justified claim: parameterized representation saves tokens only for single-slot patterns where per-slot concrete value >> slot name+3; multi-slot overhead dominates even when total length is long.
